# Project Brief

What this project is, the problem it solves, and its domain language. The non-derivable "why", not the "how".

## What it is

- A local web tool that maps a scattered music collection onto a manually organized library: it finds what is missing, copies it in one keystroke, fills missing years, files by style, and edits cues/loops with a waveform on a Traktor (NML) collection.
- One user, one machine, one collection. Python 3.12 + Flask serves it on port 8765; the frontend is vanilla TypeScript bundled by esbuild, no framework.

## Why it exists

- A large DJ collection lives in dozens of folders ("éparpillé") next to a hand-sorted library ("Source Data"). The gap between the two was maintained by hand — find, copy, tag, file.
- Nothing was ever deleted: a removed file goes to `<source>/_trash/<date>/`, never to the bin.
- Years and genres are metadata the tool writes to the files themselves (ID3/FLAC), with a journal as the only undo path.

## Domain language

| Term | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| Source Data | The organized library the collection converges on. One folder per style. |
| Éparpillé | A file outside Source Data, waiting to be filed. The left column. |
| Tranche | A 5-year band of a style folder: `techno_acid_1990`. `trancheOf(y) = y - y%5`. |
| Style | The folder's declared genre, parsed from its name (`^([a-z]+(?:_[a-z]+)*?)(?:_(\d{4}))?$`). Derived from the disk, never a maintained list. |
| Jumeau (twin) | The copy of a file already filed in Source Data. |
| Doublon / homonyme probable | Exact same name / same length ±2 s with a fuzzy name. Three LED colours tell them apart. |
| Pastille « déjà rangé » | The badge on an épars whose twin already exists under the active source filter. |
| Beatgrid / grille | BPM + phase + downbeats, detected or entered, written into the NML as `TEMPO` + `CUE_V2 TYPE=4`. |
| Cue / loop | A marker or a loop on the waveform, slots A–H, stored in the NML. |
| NML / collection.nml | Traktor's collection file. The app parses it, adds tracks to it, writes cues and grids into it. |
| Journal | `data/journal.json`, append-only, one line per operation. Not the write journal. |
| Write journal | `data/year_apply_journal.jsonl` / `data/style_apply_journal.jsonl`: the only undo path for tag writes, shared by the scripts and the palette. |
| Certain / à revue / introuvable | The three verdicts of the year consolidation. Only `certain` may be written to a file. |
| EPIC | The unit of evolution: one file in `docs/superpowers/epics/` plus a line in its index. |
| Trash | `<source>/_trash/<date>/`. The replacement for deleting audio. |

## Key features

- Sync: scan the scattered folders, spot missing and duplicated files, copy into the right sub-folder with `F5`.
- Doubles: groups of versions of one track, quality arbitration, the losers filed into `_trash/`.

- Styles: a keyboard palette that picks the style and computes the destination folder, then writes the tag right away.
- Playlists: create, rate, export by hard links, with a Traktor import badge.
- Cue editor: waveform, cues A–H, loops, zoom, beatgrid, and a grid written back into the NML.

The HTTP API surface: its style, the main resources, and the contracts.

- A flat REST-ish surface served by Flask, all of it in `app.py`. No versioning, no base path, no prefix.

- Playlists and ratings: `/playlists`, `/ratings`, `/audio`.
- Traktor: `/api/nml/status`, `/api/track/match`, `/api/track/add`, `/api/track/cues`, `/api/track/grid`, `/api/beatgrid`, `/api/track/analyze`.

## Contracts

- There is no OpenAPI spec and no schema file: `app.py` is the contract, and the frontend calls it from `static/src/api.ts` (a fetch wrapper with a network retry).
- The routes that write a tag follow one grammar, whatever the route: validate → confine the path to the configured roots → write the old value to the journal → write the frame → re-read the file. A write that fails is reported, never silently swallowed.
- A write also patches the scan index in the same request and answers `cache_updated`; without it the screen would serve the value from before the write.
- Errors: `jsonify({'ok': False, 'error': …})` with the matching status code. A corrupt JSON file in `data/` is never a 500: the default is returned and the incident is journalled.
- The client is told which half of the pair was written: the copy route answers `style`, `style_writes` and `style_error` separately, so a failed tag never blocks the copy.

The visual language: the design system, tokens, and UI conventions. What it looks like, not how it is coded.

- No component library and no CSS framework. The design system is a set of CSS layers plus a small vocabulary of shared components.

- Every colour, spacing and typography value is a CSS variable declared in `static/styles/tokens.css`, and only there. A token declared twice is a bug.
- `npm run audit:css` reports the CSS that no longer matches anything. It is a report, not a fix: every dead rule has to be checked by hand.

## Components

- The shared components are the modal, the dialog, the toast, the filter chip, the empty panel, the file row, the source tree node and the style palette. `static/src/render/` holds one factory per page and per shared component.
- One focus grammar everywhere: a 2 px accent box, a 4 px bar and a tinted background. It was measured, not chosen by eye — the panel contrast went from 3.38:1 to 11.45:1.

- The bar is measured: focus visibility, contrast, and the legend layout are verified by the headless harnesses (`scripts/measure_focus_visibility.py`, `scripts/measure_legend.py`), which compute what the browser actually renders.
